content:
chen: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak, we're seeing a p95 tail spike for streamed responses on small prompts (<= 24 tokens). Not obvious from perf dashboards yet.

sam: ugh. saw anything in the rollout notes? which kernel change specifically?

chen: it was the fallback path: prefer small-kernel-evict for kernels that support int8-optimized matmul. config change: kernel_priority: [fast_small, generic, fallback]. rolled at ~04:00 UTC.

nina: interesting — streaming + small prompts interacts badly with batching: continuous-batcher sometimes holds a single stream request to wait for a joiner, then partial-decode path triggers kernel handoff and we pay ~3 extra ms per token on p95.

radev: can you paste a trace? perf-bot: flamegraph attached in thread (summary).

perf-bot: summary: sample=10k requests (small prompt), baseline (old kernel_priority) p95=48ms, current p95=72ms. p50 ~ unchanged. Hotspot: kernel selection latency (+14ms) + KV cache miss penalty (+8ms) on partial decode warms.

sam: that smells like two things: (1) the kernel decision code path is doing expensive compatibility checks synchronously, (2) kv-cache warmup is being deferred on held-back streams.

chen: yes. here's a minimal repro we ran locally:

```bash
# reproduce: 10k small-stream requests
wrk -t8 -c100 -d30s "http://localhost:8080/gen?stream=true&model=redwood-small" --script small_stream.lua
```

And an excerpt from the runtime log where the stall happens: 

```
[2026-02-11T04:12:03Z] decode: partial-decode-start req=12345 kernel=fast_small checks=5
[2026-02-11T04:12:03Z] kernel: falling back to generic due to layout-mismatch req=12345 cost=12ms
[2026-02-11T04:12:03Z] kvcache: miss warmup queued req=12345
[2026-02-11T04:12:03Z] stream: flush heldback req=12345 delay=8ms
```

nina: ok. two parallel experiments I'd run: (A) short-circuit kernel compatibility checks for already-profiled model+seqlen combos (cache results per route), (B) prefetch KV warmup for streams once admission happens (i.e., when request enters queue rather than when decode starts).

radev: +1 for profiling the kernel check itself. I think it does a memcpy-check on tensor layout that can be avoided if we store kernel-capability bitsets per model-shape.

sam: for the batcher heuristics, can we relax holdback for streams when estimated join time > X ms? i.e., switch to early-send for small prompts where waiting is counterproductive. We already have a token_budget target — maybe set sample dependent thresholds for stream vs non-stream.

chen: proposal: 3-prong change set
1) kernel-decision cache: map<model,seqlen,hw> -> chosen_kernel (ttl 60s)
2) kv warmup on admission: fire async kv.prefetch(req.route) when admitted to coalescing queue
3) stream holdback rule: if queueing.delay_estimate > 4ms or expected_joiners < 1 then early-send partial-decode

nina: sounds reasonable. rough numbers we saw in local A/B: implementing (1) reduced kernel-decision overhead by ~9ms p95; (2) kv warmup cut kv penalty from +8ms -> +2ms; (3) holdback relaxation traded a tiny throughput drop (~1.5%) for p95 latency improvement of ~10ms on small prompts.

radev: risk: early-send increases token churn for the GPU (more tiny kernels) — need to measure perf per-gpu util. Also need to ensure early partial-decode doesn't break deterministic output ordering.

chen: good point. check-list before rollout:
- add kernel-decision cache + metrics (cache-hit ratio)
- make kv.prefetch async and idempotent, add prefetch histogram
- implement holdback heuristic behind flag rollouts + telemetry: percent_in_early_send, p95 by prompt-len

sam: can someone spin a canary with 10% traffic and record: p50/p95/p99, gpu_util, tokens/sec, kv.prefetch hit ratio? Also add a synthetic tiny-prompt stream job to CI e2e so we don't regress this again.

nina: I'll own the synthetic job and metrics dashboard. chen/radev can own the runtime changes. I'll pair on the telemetry schema.

chen: thanks — will push a draft PR with the kernel cache and prefetch bits today. tagging: @sam FYI for rollout plan.

sam: awesome. please add an annotated flamegraph to the PR showing before/after. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf test queued: run-id=perf-2245678912-1, will post results to thread when done.

radev: if perf test looks good we can toggle the feature-flag for 10% traffic and keep it running for 24h before enlarging.

chen: noted. I'll update here with PR link and perf attachments.

(edited)
